title: Item Limits, Coverage Billing and Earliest Ship Dates in the PAP Supply Replenishment Program
content:
## 1. Limits per item

Under the PAP Supply Replenishment Program each item follows its own limit of a number of units per number of months, measured on the schedule's period basis.

**Covered period of a line.** The clause "the units shipped on one line cover the units divided by the limit's quantity, multiplied by the limit's months, in calendar months from the ship date, and the covered-through date is the day before the same day of the month that many months later (month-end fallback)" is **no longer in force** for a coverage-billed disposable-filter line booked under the current filter rule, for a no-charge reship, which counts toward no limit, and for a standing-order line on the Self-Pay Supply Subscription, which has no unit limits; those lines take the covered-through dates their own rules state. Every other line that an item limit dates remains under this clause.

*Worked example of the clause where it remains in force (hypothetical limit and dates):* a line of 6 units of an item limited to 2 units per 1 month covers 6 divided by 2, multiplied by 1, which is 3 calendar months. Shipped on 10 January, its covered-through date is the day before 10 April: 9 April.

## 2. Months per line

One line may cover at most the schedule's maximum months per shipment, except an item whose own period is longer, which ships one period (the limit's quantity of units) at a time.

## 3. Earliest ship date

A new line of an item ships no earlier than the schedule's ship-window days before the current supply of the item runs out, counting back calendar days from the item's current covered-through date with the boundary day included; travel adds the schedule's extra early days for travel where that value is above 0.

The item's current covered-through date is the latest covered-through date among the enrollment's shipped lines of that item up to the handling date, leaving out any line a payer has taken back; it is empty when the item has never shipped. The test is made on the system's shipment records for the same enrollment and the same item, before the line ships.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, a 10-day window, no travel):* the item's current covered-through date is the 25th of a month. Counting back 10 calendar days with the boundary day included, the earliest ship day is the 15th. A line shipping on the 15th meets the rule; a line shipping on the 14th is too early. With a hypothetical travel allowance of 14 days on top, the earliest ship day moves 24 calendar days back from the 25th, to the 1st.

## 4. Missed cycles

Quantities not shipped in an earlier period are never added to a later line unless the schedule allows missed-cycle quantities to be added.

## 5. Allowed amount

The allowed amount of a coverage-billed line is the quantity multiplied by the item's fee-schedule amount, multiplied by the coverage class's allowed percentage of the fee schedule and divided by 100, rounded to the cent half up.

*Worked example (hypothetical figures):* 2 units of an item with a fee-schedule amount of 10.25, under a coverage class allowing 80 percent: 2 multiplied by 10.25 is 20.50; 20.50 multiplied by 80 and divided by 100 is 16.40. The allowed amount is 16.40.

## 6. Units beyond the limit

Units beyond the limit are not billed to coverage; where the schedule allows items beyond the schedule to be sold at self-pay prices, the patient may buy them as a self-pay line.

## 7. Enrollment status

Items ship only while the enrollment is active. The status is read from the enrollment record in the system before the line ships.

| Enrollment status | Items ship? |
|---|---|
| active | yes |
| pending enrollment, on hold or cancelled | no |
